newsitem.title: USA: Bausch & Lomb not seeking to sell units.
newsitem.headline: Bausch & Lomb not seeking to sell units.

text.p: Bausch & Lomb is not seeking to divest its non-core businesses, Chief Exeuctive William M. Carpenter said on Wednesday.

Asked during a news conference whether the company's restructuring plan involved the sale of any non-core operations, Carpenter said those units were independently managed and "financially accretive" to the company's first-quarter results.
Still, he said the company, which makes contact lenses and other optical products, might consider selling a non-core unit if it was worth more to another party.
Asked if Bausch & Lomb is seeking such offers, Carpenter said, "We're not actively seeking any divestiture."
Earlier Wednesday the company detailed "a major restructuring plan that is expected to result in annual savings of more than $100 million in 1999."
Carpenter said the base year for expected restructuring savings was 1995.
The savings "are incremental to annual savings of $50 million that the company had identified through projects announced in early 1996," the company said.
"These existing plans are on track," it added.

The latest restructuring resulted in a $7.7 million charge against first-quarter profits and the promise of more charges later this year. The first quarter also had a $6.8 million charge for the previously announced discontinuing of certain sunglass lines.
"If Bausch & Lomb didn't have some off-balance sheet charges, it wouldn't be Bausch & Lomb," Derby Securities analyst Otto Grote said.

Describing the restructurings as "the unwinding of a long process of trying to compensate" for the company's loss of contact lens leadership to Johnson & Johnson a decade ago, Grote said Bausch & Lomb is "doing the right thing."
However, he does not "think this will be the last reorganization, the last writeoff.
"The question is, what else do they have?"
